event.summary: Retaining tmux-era screen fixtures remains justified for surviving host agents
event.detail: Reviewed commits: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333 and 08399d092d20815ced6619c26df2391944ae2b4a. TLDR: considered whether the revised reason for keeping old screen captures incorrectly preserves obsolete terminal behavior. The edits only clarify documentation; they neither change fixture data nor require a current terminal to pretend it is tmux. Details: the complete assigned patches modify module prose and repaint-test prose, leaving executable assertions unchanged. At 08399d092d20815ced6619c26df2391944ae2b4a, SPEC_impl.md:2187-2200 says the child now receives Farhelm terminal variables, and explicitly states: 'until 2026-11 the child got `TERM_PROGRAM=tmux`, the private server’s version and a placeholder `TMUX` that held such an autostart back, and a host started then keeps that environment until its agent is restarted.' Its status contract at SPEC_impl.md:4202-4207 explicitly retains pre-November captures for agents in terminal hosts started before 0.36.0. The repaint test at screen_fixtures.rs:488-606 independently checks that captured text survives the current emulator and its status reader; it does not replay live programs or change terminal environments. docs/agent-screen-fixtures.md:33-37 at 4b489b4f2eeade14f119b186ecb16eeaaf027021 gives the same retained-host rationale. Suggested bucket: other (explanatory test documentation). Confidence: confirmed by patch and source contract; no execution and no claim of newly observing installed vendor behavior. proposed_drop: no changed runtime or assertion behavior, and retained old-agent coverage agrees with the explicit compatibility contract. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Could-be-highest: no; the comments neither remove coverage nor introduce a security or user-work mutation path. Historical release-version attribution was not independently audited; no contrary source premise was found.

event.summary: Inspection-helper wording still describes its private terminal-host path
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 4b489b4f2eeade14f119b186ecb16eeaaf027021 (scripts/agent_screen_host.py:1-15, scripts/agent-tui.py:4-12, scripts/capture-agent-screens.py:6-13); also d751ff1633bb479c7bf53920f2e4ea4ba932a1c2 (scripts/capture-agent-screens.py:521-522). TLDR: considered whether removing the distinction between new and old terminals falsely promises isolation or a production-like terminal environment, and whether generalizing the timeout comment weakens a lifecycle guarantee. The changed text agrees with the existing implementation; no executable behavior changes in these hunks. Details: at 4b489b4f2eeade14f119b186ecb16eeaaf027021, agent_screen_host.py:66-74 strips ambient FARHELM_ variables, TMUX/TMUX_PANE and named outer-agent markers; HostRun.start at :98-139 creates a random /tmp/fh-tui- directory and launches the explicitly selected farhelm internal agent-screen with that environment. crates/farhelm-supervisor/src/agent_screen.rs:154-200 passes its private run_dir to spawn_host and builds the program environment with the same crate::service::host_child_env used for production hosts; it adopts the host as Fresh with the normal HostTerminal runtime. Its module contract at :9-25 names the shared emulator query path and private state directory. SPEC.md:2899-2906 and SPEC_impl.md:2187-2200 specify Farhelm terminal variables for all new launches, with older hosts retaining their launch environment. At d751ff1633bb479c7bf53920f2e4ea4ba932a1c2, reach_prompt at capture-agent-screens.py:507-549 checks both child exit and deadline before answering trust and taking continue; the generalized comment preserves the actual guard and does not assert an unverified new vendor behavior. Suggested bucket: other (development-tool explanatory text). Confidence: confirmed by source; no runtime or real-agent observations. proposed_drop: wording-only changes preserve the inspected isolation, environment, and timeout contracts. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Could-be-highest: no; no changed cleanup, credential handling or process-targeting route exists in these patches. This does not audit unrelated pre-existing helper behavior.
